title: Thicken+
tagline: Onshape's Thicken, with the two thicknesses named 'toward reference' and 'away from reference' instead of by the face normal -- the boolean step unchanged.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: The built-in Thicken's Thickness 1 goes along the face normal, so the same feature thickens outward on one model and inward on another. Thicken+ decides per surface body which way is 'toward the reference' and puts the Toward thickness there. Everything else -- New / Add / Remove / Intersect, merge scope -- is the built-in.
useWhen: Surfaces of mixed orientation must thicken the same way
A surface's normal may flip upstream
You want a clear error where a thicken would fold, with its location
slides.caption: Left: both sheets thicken toward the reference whatever their normals. Right: the curvature check.

slides.title: Why a reference instead of a flip

points.head: A flip is about a normal
points.body: 'Front', 'opposite direction', 'Thickness 1' all mean: relative to the normal -- and normals change freely upstream.

points.head: A reference is about the model
points.body: Pick geometry on the side you mean. The choice survives any change of orientation.

points.head: Drop-in
points.body: With no reference, the feature behaves exactly like the built-in.

slides.title: The dialog
params: New / Add / Remove / Intersect -- the built-in boolean step, unchanged.
Surfaces or faces; each owner body is thickened on its own side.
Geometry on the side to thicken toward -- best a mate connector or vertex near the surface. Empty = along the normals.
The arrow: exchange the two thicknesses.
Check curvature (on): report where a concave radius is smaller than the thickness. Print details.

slides.title: Example: opposite normals, same result
slides.head: Test T2: sheets at z +50 and -50 with opposite normals, reference at the centre, Toward 2, Away 3
slides.body: Both sheets put 2 mm toward the centre and 3 mm away: top z 48..53, bottom z -53..-48 -- mirror images, although their normals point opposite ways. T3 (Swap sides) gives 47..52 / -52..-47. T6: Add into a cube, 5 mm up -> one part, volume 1 018 000 mm3.

points.head: Why thickens fail
points.body: Thickening toward a concave side by more than its radius turns the offset inside out.

points.head: Found before the kernel fails
points.body: Each face is sampled on a 9 x 9 grid; the first place that would fold is marked red, with its radius.

points.head: Tests T4 / T5
points.body: Half cylinder r 10 thickened toward its axis: 15 mm -> the error with location; 5 mm -> a clean shell.

items.head: Use it instead of Thicken downstream
items.body: Surfaces from Split+, Mutual Trim+ or Offset+ keep their inputs' orientation; Thicken+ does not care which way they face.

items.head: Faces stay named through the boolean
items.body: towardFaces / awayFaces / sideFaces still resolve after Add merges the result into a part.

items.head: Orientation does not apply
items.body: Its outputs are solids, which always face outward -- Orient to reference is for surfaces.
